subject.title: contextPruning (mode: cache-ttl) never fires on OpenAI models: isCacheTtlEligibleProvider excludes OpenAI, so the idle-gap tool-result firebreak is dead for the highest-volume provider

question: Should native OpenAI cache-TTL pruning use the existing cache-TTL eligibility path, a retention-aware OpenAI variant, or a new provider-agnostic pruning mode?
rationale: Source inspection proves OpenAI is currently excluded, but enabling pruning changes existing OpenAI session-context behavior and prior ClawSweeper review of the linked PR flagged OpenAI retention semantics as a maintainer choice.

options.title: Approve retention-aware OpenAI pruning
options.body: Keep the linked PR as the fix path, but require explicit OpenAI TTL/session semantics, focused tests, and redacted native idle-gap proof before merge.

options.title: Prefer provider-agnostic pruning
options.body: Replace the eligibility-gate approach with a provider-agnostic pruning mode so stale tool-result cleanup no longer depends on prompt-cache provider eligibility.

options.title: Keep OpenAI excluded for now
options.body: Document OpenAI cache-TTL pruning as unsupported and leave this issue open or close only if maintainers intentionally reject the behavior.

recommendation.title: Approve retention-aware OpenAI pruning
recommendation.body: Keep the linked PR as the fix path, but require explicit OpenAI TTL/session semantics, focused tests, and redacted native idle-gap proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the cache-TTL pruning mode and prompt-caching docs, so he is the best routed owner for the product semantics decision among the traced people.
